text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000376 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation in every complexity band, but the few documented 99215 claims support the billed level, so documentation is too thin to call this upcoding or a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share runs above the all-provider rate in every chronic-condition band, including patients with 0 or 1 conditions. Sampled low-complexity 99215s such as C0187843 (J06.9 only), C0188038 (Z09 only) and C0187944 (N39.0 only) are the kind of visits that would usually not need high-complexity MDM. That pattern is consistent with upcoding. Some high-complexity patients are present, though, such as C0187899 and C0188001, and the 99215 share does rise with complexity as it should. The records review does not settle the question: only 5 documented 99215 claims came back, all supported at high MDM, and there is one 99214 mismatch (C0188087). The small number of notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim is weak evidence that the notes may not match what happened, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims and check those notes for templated or cloned MDM language."}
